- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) or shows strong reversal, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for mean reversion.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing early trend reversals; adjust by adding 1–2 days of sentiment-weighted momentum to forecast tail.
- If sentiment history includes multiple -1.00 entries, model underperforms in early period; boost forecast for first 5–7 days of horizon by 2–4% to capture sentiment-driven bounce.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above 75% of historical mean, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.
